newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil makes contact with isolated Amazon tribe.
newsitem.headline: Brazil makes contact with isolated Amazon tribe.

text.p: A tribe of Brazilian Indians who have been pushed deep into the Amazon rainforest after violent clashes with the outside world have established contact with a team of government officials, a newspaper reported on Sunday.

The Corubo Indians were located in the Javari River valley, near Brazil's border with Peru and Colombia, where they, and at least four other isolated tribes, have fought with loggers, O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper said.
Sidney Possuelo, a specialist leading a team from the government's National Indian Foundation (Funai), said contact had been made with the Corubos to ensure their survival.
The newspaper said 40 members of the tribe were massacred by settlers in 1928 and since then at least two officials seeking to establish contact have been killed by the Corubos.

The meeting took place on Oct. 15 when the Corubos, who had been left presents of pans and knives for over several days, emerged from the forest in response to calls from Indians who speak similar languages, the newspaper said.

The next day, 20 Corubos visited Possuelo and meetings continue to take place. The Funai team sank a boat at the mouth of a tributary leading to the tribe's land to prevent loggers and settlers from reaching the area.
Government officials believe 59 Indian tribes remain isolated from the rest of society in Brazil, O Estado said.
